answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally issued credential or a bond that is forfeited when independent audits catch fabricated activity. New accounts gain influence only as they build a verifiable history; copied behavior may echo across accounts, but correlated claims trigger scrutiny rather than multiplying trust. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must obtain many credentials or tie up many bonds, while a jetty of low-trust identities cannot move the market signal without risking losses.
